script.title: He Hated the Eiffel Tower, So He Ate Lunch Inside It
script.hook_text: He hated it, then dined there
sentences: One writer who hated the Eiffel Tower supposedly lunched there daily.
It was the centrepiece of the 1889 World's Fair in Paris.
No structure had ever reached 300 metres, and many believed it impossible.
A "Committee of Three Hundred" formed against it, one member per metre of its height.
Their petition called it "useless and monstrous", like "a gigantic black smokestack".
Among them was writer Guy de Maupassant.
Yet, the story goes, he ate lunch in the tower's restaurant every day, the one place in Paris where it was not visible.
Would you have signed that petition?
script.description:
Paris's top artists signed a petition against the Eiffel Tower.
One of them supposedly ate lunch inside it every day.
claims_en: Guy de Maupassant supposedly ate lunch in the tower's restaurant every day because it was the one place in Paris where the tower was not visible.
The tower was the centrepiece of the 1889 World's Fair.
No structure had ever been built to a height of 300 m, and many people believed it was impossible.
A "Committee of Three Hundred" (one member for each metre of the tower's height) was formed against it.
The petition called it "useless and monstrous" and compared it to "a gigantic black smokestack".
Guy de Maupassant was among the committee.
